name: Multiple Sclerosis
summary: Physiotherapy supports mobility, balance, strength, fatigue management and activity throughout the disease, with exercise adapted to heat sensitivity and fatigue and coordinated with the neurology team.

redFlags: New or sudden neurological symptoms (possible relapse)
Sudden visual loss or severe vertigo
Bladder retention or new bladder or bowel control loss
Fever or infection with worsening weakness
Marked worsening of spasticity with pain
firstSteps: Record symptoms, fatigue pattern, falls, walking and balance.
Screen for relapse symptoms and heat sensitivity.
Teach pacing and start gentle, achievable exercise.
selfCare: Regular activity with pacing and rest breaks

stages.label: Start: assess and set up
stages.goal: Exercise is safe and beneficial in MS, but heat and fatigue can worsen symptoms temporarily, so the programme is paced and cool.
do: Record symptoms, fatigue pattern, falls, walking and balance.
Screen for relapse symptoms and heat sensitivity.
Teach pacing and start gentle, achievable exercise.
Assess: Symptoms, relapses and fatigue pattern

stages.label: Treat: build capacity
stages.goal: Treat the most limiting problems: walking, balance, spasticity and fatigue.
dose: Aerobic training: 10 to 30 minutes at moderate effort, 2 to 3 days a week, in cool conditions.
Resistance training: 2 to 3 sets of 8 to 12 repetitions, 2 days a week.
Balance and gait training: 10 to 20 minutes, 3 or more days a week.
Stretching for spasticity: daily, holding 30 seconds.
moveOn: Add challenge to balance and gait in safe settings
Adapt the plan after a relapse and return gradually

stages.label: Progress and self-manage
stages.goal: Adapt during and after relapses and coordinate with the neurology team.
when: Add challenge to balance and gait in safe settings
do: Regular activity with pacing and rest breaks
dose: Increase duration before intensity and rest well between sessions.
Progress balance difficulty safely near support.
Reduce and rebuild after a relapse.
